question: In March 2025, ISRO advanced in developing which engine for LVM3?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Semicryogenic engine**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **semicryogenic engine** is a critical propulsion technology being developed by the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** for its launch vehicles, especially the **Launch Vehicle Mark-3 (LVM3)**.
 
• This engine uses a combination of **liquid oxygen (LOX) as the oxidizer** and **kerosene** as the fuel, which makes it efficient and capable of producing high thrust.
 
• Compared to cryogenic engines, which use liquid hydrogen as fuel, semicryogenic engines are more cost-effective due to the easier availability and storage of kerosene.
 
• The development of this engine is part of ISRO's goal to enhance the payload capacity of its launch vehicles and reduce reliance on foreign propulsion systems for advanced missions.
 
• Once operational, the semicryogenic engine is expected to significantly boost India’s space exploration capabilities by enabling the launch of heavier satellites at a reduced cost.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Semicryogenic Engine Characteristics:**

 
 
• This engine operates at **extremely low temperatures**, with liquid oxygen stored at approximately -183°C.
 
• It produces a **high thrust-to-weight ratio**, making it suitable for lifting heavy payloads into orbit.
 
• The use of kerosene as fuel results in reduced operational costs and easier handling compared to cryogenic fuels like liquid hydrogen.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Engine Types:**
 
 
• **Electric Jet Engine:** Used in aircraft, it relies on electrical energy to drive a turbine for propulsion, making it unsuitable for space applications due to power constraints.
 
• **Turbo Plasma Engine:** Primarily hypothetical or experimental, not yet widely used in space propulsion systems.
 
• **Liquid Booster:** Refers to boosters using liquid propellant but does not describe a specific engine type like the semicryogenic engine.
 
 
 
• **ISRO’s Future Missions:**
 
 
• ISRO plans to use semicryogenic engines in upcoming launch vehicles like the **Unified Launch Vehicle (ULV)** to replace current systems in the LVM3.
 
• These engines will be pivotal in **Gaganyaan**, India’s first manned space mission, and other interplanetary exploration missions.
 
 
 
• **Global Perspective:**
 
 
• Space agencies like **NASA** and **Roscosmos** have used similar technologies in their launch vehicles, providing a proven track record for semicryogenic engines.
 
• India’s development of this technology will enhance its position in the **global space industry**, promoting self-reliance and competitiveness.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **ISRO’s Achievements:**

 
 
• ISRO has already developed and operationalized cryogenic engines, used in its GSLV series for launching heavy satellites.
 
• The semicryogenic engine is a step forward in improving fuel efficiency and reducing costs for heavier payloads.
 
 
 
• **Cost-Effectiveness:**
 
 
• Using kerosene as fuel is more economical and environmentally friendly compared to traditional cryogenic fuels.
 
 
 
• **Strategic Importance:**
 
 
• Developing indigenous propulsion systems like the semicryogenic engine will reduce India’s dependency on foreign technology and enhance national security.
